# PowerPlay v2.1.3 — Fire TV

*Plex-focused Fire TV app · Fire OS 7/8 · ARMv7*

## Changes in this release

- Generalize the **opt-in original Pro Logic I-compatible Lt/Rt output** from the v2.1.2 Dolby-specific recovery path to all multichannel formats the existing bundled ExoPlayer FFmpeg renderer can decode, including AC3/E-AC3, DTS/DTS-HD, TrueHD, AAC, Opus, FLAC, ALAC, Vorbis, and other supported FFmpeg audio types.
- When enabled, ask hardware decoders for the source's full **3–12 channel PCM** output, and retry once through the bundled FFmpeg ExoPlayer renderer if the decoder reduces the source channel count (for example 7.1 → 5.1 or 5.1 → stereo). DTS's existing direct-to-FFmpeg decoding policy is preserved. No new native libraries or streaming transcodes.
- Expand the streaming matrix processor from **1–8 to 1–12 PCM channels** and accept **8-bit, 16-bit, packed 24-bit, signed 32-bit, and floating-point PCM**, maintaining the original low-allocation real-time audio loop.
- Preserve front left/right and center; fold all rear/side speaker beds into the original Pro Logic **single band-limited mono surround**, encoded into Lt/Rt with the 90-degree phase relationship. For common 7.1.2 / 7.1.4-style beds, fold extra height pairs into front or mono-surround components with extra headroom rather than discarding their audio.
- Continue to **leave ordinary stereo and already matrix-encoded Lt/Rt untouched** and omit discrete LFE, consistent with conventional Lt/Rt downmixes. Pro Logic remains disabled by default and audio passthrough is suppressed only when matrix processing is opted in. Video decoding, application identity, PowerLink and Home Assistant integrations are unchanged.
- Add decoder-policy and PCM processing regressions for DTS, AAC, TrueHD, Opus, 12-channel float, 24-bit PCM, front-height and rear-height folding, and original Pro Logic rear-phase behavior. Existing performance-overlay telemetry still indicates the **actual PCM channels received**, two-channel output and matrix workload.

## Compatibility and validation

- **Any audio format** means any decodable stream with usable PCM output, **not** an unconditional guarantee for every codec/profile, unusual channel layout, proprietary object-based stream, or source exceeding 12 channels. Pro Logic I cannot recreate Atmos/DTS:X objects or discrete 7.1 from a stereo matrix. For 9–12 channels, the current Media3 AudioProcessor API provides channel count but not exact speaker labels, so unusual channel arrangements use a conservative best-effort fold.
- On-device Fire TV tests are still required for Dolby 5.1, DTS 5.1, 7.1 and available height-format samples. The performance overlay's **Active – Lt/Rt** and channel counts prove PowerPlay encoded PCM, not that the TV/optical converter preserves stereo phase or the Pioneer receiver steers correctly.
- Where decoded multichannel PCM cannot be obtained, preserve compatibility and report the actual output instead of falsely claiming matrix conversion. FFmpeg software decoding may increase Fire Stick CPU utilization; watch the overlay's real-time processing budget and audio underrun count.
